details:
Even more arbitrary UI/X changes abound. Now, in addition to a less useful UX that requires more steps to find useful information and removes at-a-glance utility, we have a jarring new default accent colour and palette. One of the first things you learn not to do when designing an experience: Thou shalt not add unneeded steps to a user workflow, nor shall ye remove or relocate features without cause. 

The best user experience is one that is so frictionless the user doesn't think about how they are interacting with it, it's just there.

There was a lot of potential for the redesign to strengthen the features and layouts that existed, but the ball was dropped in a big way and additional new updates seem to sort of double down on it. 

I assume this is to encourage users to buy the eye-wateringly awful colour palettes and themes, though thankfully the ability to create a custom palette still exists, which is a blessing. The new themes that other users apply to themselves being visible to other people really only serves to make things less readable. Also, even though there is a higher contrast with the new default colours, the forced change is still jarring and distracting. Meanwhile, we've still got a nested slide menu for the camera that makes operation a chore. 

While the "legacy" default also still exists, it's overridden by the new default upon launching the update. In addition to never removing functionality via an update, existing preferences and selections should never be automatically changed by an update. This is typically only acceptable in the case that the feature is fully deprecated and that the user is informed. But that's just not the case.
title: Arbitrary UI changes and the Golden Rule
